[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fly fishing involves casting a lightweight lure called a fly that imitates natural food sources of fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Spinner baits create a spinning motion to attract fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Factors to consider for choosing the right fly include target species, water type, time of year, and water conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Popular fly types for beginners include dry flies (e.g., Elk Hair Caddis, Stimulator, Blue Wing Olive), nymphs (e.g., Hare's Ear, Pheasant Tail, Gold-Ribbed Hare's Ear), and streamers (e.g., Woolly Bugger, Muddler Minnow).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For Lake Michigan trout in the spring, expect hatches of midges, black stoneflies, and early mayflies like the Hendrickson and March Brown.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Trout in Lake Michigan tend to move into shallower waters (10-20 feet) during spring as the water warms up.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended dry flies for Lake Michigan trout include Midges and Mayflies (Hendrickson, March Brown).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended nymphs for Lake Michigan trout include stonefly nymphs and mayfly nymphs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Streamers can be effective for trout, especially in spring when they are aggressive and baitfish are active.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested streamer patterns include Woolly Bugger and Muddler Minnow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for using a streamer include choosing a baitfish-imitating pattern, using a sink-tip or sinking line, varying the retrieve, and fishing
